title: Schema Migrations and Application Releases knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is a useful migration strategy for an application with old and new code running together?
options: Expand the schema, deploy compatible code, backfill and verify, then remove old structures later.
Drop the old column before the new code is deployed.
Change production without testing populated data.
Combine every change into one irreversible operation.
questions.answer_key: Expand the schema, deploy compatible code, backfill and verify, then remove old structures later.
questions.explanation: Expand/contract migrations reduce compatibility risk during rolling deployment and should be rehearsed with representative data.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports a correct implementation of schema migrations and application releases?
options: Concatenate user input into SQL and remove permission checks
Assume one successful example proves security and recovery
Apply the largest possible change before collecting a baseline
Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.answer_key: Define the expected behavior and prerequisites, make the smallest change in an isolated environment, then verify both success and an important edge case.
questions.explanation: A controlled example makes the prerequisites and expected behavior explicit. Verification of an edge case helps show whether the idea behind schema migrations and application releases is understood.

questions.prompt: When an example related to schema migrations and application releases produces an unexpected result, what is the strongest next step?
options: Grant administrator privileges to every application role
Ignore the returned result and assume the write succeeded
Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
Disable constraints and retry until the command succeeds
questions.answer_key: Capture the exact error and context, inspect relevant state or logs, test one hypothesis at a time, and document the verified result.
questions.explanation: Database troubleshooting should be evidence-led and performed with suitable permissions. Broad privileges or disabling integrity checks may hide the cause and create new failures.
